content.title: Anticoagulation recommendations for pulmonary embolism (PE)
content.summary: Guidance on duration and extension of anticoagulation after PE, dose adjustments for extended therapy, alternative agents when oral anticoagulation is not possible, and follow-up monitoring.

recommendations.statement: Therapeutic anticoagulation for ≥ 3 months is recommended for all patients with PE.
Discontinuation of anticoagulation after 3 months is recommended for patients with first PE/VTE secondary to a major transient/reversible risk factor.

Extension of anticoagulation beyond 3 months is recommended for patients with recurrent VTE (that is, with at least one previous episode of PE or DVT) not related to a major transient or reversible risk factor.
Oral anticoagulant treatment with a VKA for an indefinite period is recommended for patients with antiphospholipid antibody syndrome.
Extended oral anticoagulation of indefinite duration should be considered for patients with a first episode of PE and no identifiable risk factor.

Extended oral anticoagulation of indefinite duration should be considered for patients with a first episode of PE associated with a persistent risk factor other than antiphospholipid antibody syndrome.
Extended oral anticoagulation of indefinite duration should be considered for patients with a first episode of PE associated with a minor transient or reversible risk factor.

If extended oral anticoagulation is decided after PE in a patient without cancer, a reduced dose of the NOACs apixaban (2.5 mg b.i.d.) or rivaroxaban (10 mg o.d.) should be considered after 6 months of therapeutic anticoagulation.
In patients who refuse or are unable to tolerate any form of oral anticoagulants, aspirin or sulodexide may be considered for extended VTE prophylaxis.
Follow-up: For patients receiving extended anticoagulation, reassess drug tolerance and adherence, hepatic and renal function, and bleeding risk at regular intervals.

content.notes: Recommendations include considerations for patients with antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, cancer excluded for reduced NOAC dosing statement, and alternatives (aspirin, sulodexide) when oral anticoagulants are not tolerated.
